summary: Build drum power by preserving a dry transient path and adding density with parallel compression and/or distortion rather than crushing the only drum path.
safety_notes: Reject if cymbal harshness rises, attacks flatten, or groove loses contrast.

summary: For dense modern rock, start drum ambience from natural room or a short room/plate candidate before trying long reverbs.
safety_notes: Do not treat 0.6–1.2 s as a universal preset; use section/context A/B.

summary: Treat snare ambience as a separately designed layer: natural room, short room, plate, gated/nonlinear burst, or triggered room sample, selected by context.
safety_notes: Reject if the reverb becomes a separate wash, masks vocal consonants, or fills inter-hit space unnecessarily.

summary: Reduce cymbal contribution to the most aggressive drum compression/distortion paths when they create harshness or continuous noise.
safety_notes: Preserve kit coherence and do not make cymbals unnaturally detached.

summary: Treat rock bass as both a stable low-frequency foundation and an audible harmonic identity that must remain legible under dense guitars.
safety_notes: Reject if added top becomes fret/pick harshness or kick loses separation.

summary: Keep rhythm guitars as a midrange foundation; do not automatically scoop their mids to create space. Use level, role hierarchy, selective upper-mid/high emphasis and automation first.
safety_notes: Reject if vocal intelligibility or guitar tone identity worsens.

summary: In dense rock, keep double-tracked rhythm guitars dry or on very short/filtered ambience by default; reserve longer hall/chorus/delay for section identity and leads.
safety_notes: Long ambience is allowed when arrangement space supports it; this is not a genre prohibition.

summary: Create rock vocal size with multiple low-level, separately controllable effects rather than relying on one large reverb: short room/ER, filtered plate, tempo delay, slap and optional doubler.
safety_notes: Dry vocal anchor must remain intelligible and forward.

summary: Automate reverb and delay depth by song section: tighter verses/rock sections, larger effects in open choruses, bridges or anthemic moments when desired.
safety_notes: Do not enlarge effects merely because a section is labelled chorus; verify arrangement space and lyric clarity.

summary: Lower perceived crest factor by adding useful sustain/harmonic density and controlling local peak generators while preserving enough transient edge to define impact.
safety_notes: Reject if cymbals smear, vocal consonants flatten, groove contrast collapses, or loudness gain is the only improvement.
